evidence: .github/workflows/deploy-do.yml:220-243 — per-image Trivy CycloneDX SBOM is generated against steps.build-api.outputs.digest and attested with actions/attest-sbom (push-to-registry: true); identical steps for mct-worker (:286-304) and mct-web (:355-373)

findings.impact: The previous P1 (lockfile-only SBOM) no longer holds: every shipped image has a CycloneDX SBOM bound to its immutable digest and a registry-side attestation, so OS-package and in-image npm contents are covered for incident response.
findings.recommendation: Keep as-is; no action. Future work: validate image SBOMs before attestation (new finding) and cover third-party runtime images (new finding).
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: deploy-do.yml attests digest-bound image SBOMs via actions/attest-sbom (lines 234-243/298-304/367-373); the lockfile SBOM remains as a secondary artifact in sbom.yml:35-60.

findings.title: Unsigned Images With No Provenance/Attestation

findings.title: No version identity: no tags, no product version, no commit binding in generated artifacts
evidence: scripts/generate-sbom.mjs:300-315,325-328,441-465 — reads VERSION and GITHUB_SHA; emits metadata.component.version '<version>+<sha>' plus mct:productVersion / mct:commit properties and a deterministic serialNumber (:424-428)
scripts/validate-sbom.mjs:63-67 — CI fails if the version or mct:commit binding is missing
git tag → 0 tags; no release workflow (grep for softprops/gh release/create-release in .github/workflows → none)
docs/SBOM_PROCESS.md:65-76 and docs/RELEASING.md:52-61 — declare the commit SHA authoritative and state no git tag is required
VERSION:1 — product version is 0.1.0
findings.impact: Generated artifacts now bind to the exact commit and product version. The residual is release identity: no annotated tags and no GitHub Release exists, so SBOMs cannot be attached to a release and version history is date-based.
findings.recommendation: Owner/release decision: either cut annotated tags on prod promotion and attach the lockfile SBOM to the GitHub Release, or keep the documented commit-SHA-as-identity model and delete the remaining 'tagged release' language from CHANGELOG/RELEASING where it implies tags.
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: commit+product-version binding present in generate-sbom.mjs and enforced by validate-sbom.mjs; git tag is still empty and no release workflow exists — now a documented decision (docs/SBOM_PROCESS.md:65-76) rather than an omission.

git tag → 0; no release workflow exists

findings.recommendation: Either attest the lockfile SBOM too (actions/attest-sbom with the commit subject) or upload it to durable storage/Spaces per run; if releases are adopted, attach sbom.cdx.json to the GitHub Release (REL-P1-001).
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: the image path is fixed (digest-bound SBOM attestation, registry OCI referrer); the lockfile SBOM remains artifact-only with 30-day retention and no release attachment — documented as an accepted residual in docs/SBOM_PROCESS.md:179-186.

findings.title: Dependabot PR backlog is large and not triaged; one stale update conflicts with resolved versions

findings.note: not re-verified at 8d299b8d (reason): the PR backlog and the conflicting update are GitHub-side state, not repository state. Repository evidence is unchanged — config only, no triage automation.

findings.title: SBOM is produced as a transient artifact, not bound to a release
evidence: .github/workflows/deploy-do.yml:234-243,298-304,367-373 — actions/attest-sbom with push-to-registry: true binds each image SBOM to the pushed digest as an OCI referrer
docs/SBOM_PROCESS.md:56-63,149-158 — durable SBOM attestation complements the 30-day artifact
docs/RELEASING.md:122-129 — post-release SBOM retrieval/verification instructions
findings.impact: A shipped image's SBOM is now durable in the attestation store/registry beyond the artifact window; the residual is the lockfile SBOM, which is still transient (tracked under SBOM-P2-001).
findings.recommendation: Keep. Consider attesting the lockfile SBOM as well if a durable per-commit npm BOM is required.
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: the deploy path generates digest-bound image SBOMs and attests them to the registry.

findings.title: License exceptions are matched by license string only — documented package scope and UNKNOWN fail open
evidence: scripts/license-gate.mjs:37-39 — exceptions are keyed by entry.license only; the entry's `packages` array is never read (grep for entry.packages → no use)
scripts/license-gate.mjs:50-53 — classify() returns ok for any license string present in the exceptions map, regardless of which package declares it
security/license-policy.json:87-92 — the `UNKNOWN` exception (listed for browser-assert) makes every package with no license field pass the full-tree gate
docs/LICENSE_POLICY.md:44-45 — 'Each is scoped to the named packages only — a *different* package with the same license still fails the gate.' (contradicted by the code)

pinned dependency-review-action source src/licenses.ts (2031cfc) — unlicensed/NOASSERTION changes are reported but never added to the forbidden bucket, so the PR gate also cannot fail on a missing license
findings.impact: A new MPL-2.0, LGPL-3.0-or-later, FSL-1.1-MIT or unlicensed dependency passes the full-tree gate without review, and a package with no license field passes both gates. The compliance control does not implement the documented contract.
findings.recommendation: Match exceptions on (license string, package name): compare pkg.name against entry.packages and fail when a license is excepted for a different package. Treat UNKNOWN as a violation by default with per-package exceptions. Update the security/license-policy.json comment and docs/LICENSE_POLICY.md to match. Add unit fixtures for: new package with an excepted license string → fail; excepted package → pass; unlicensed new package → fail.
findings.note: new finding at 8d299b8d; static analysis of license-gate.mjs + policy JSON + docs. The gate could not be executed (no node runtime on the audit host), but the matching logic is a direct string lookup.

findings.title: Exception `expires` dates are documentation-only and never enforced by the gates
evidence: security/license-policy.json:66,76,84,92 — every exception carries an `expires` date (2027-10-02/03)
scripts/license-gate.mjs — no reference to `expires` anywhere (grep → none); the only stale-exception signal is when the license string disappears entirely (:127-130), which never fires for UNKNOWN
security/dependency-audit-policy.json:13-20 — allowlist entry with "expires": "2027-01-01"
scripts/audit-gate.mjs — allowlist is indexed by advisory id only (:75-77); no reference to `expires` (grep → none)
docs/DEPENDENCY_POLICY.md:30 — 'with a reason and an expiry. They never block but are always printed.'
findings.impact: Reviewed exceptions persist indefinitely after their review date with no failing signal, so an accepted risk (e.g. the UNKNOWN blanket or an unpatchable advisory) can outlive the review that justified it.
findings.recommendation: Parse `expires` (ISO date) in both gates and fail (or ::warning:: + job-summary) when past due; add a CI test with a fixture policy whose date is in the past. Keep a documented renewal process in docs/LICENSE_POLICY.md and docs/DEPENDENCY_POLICY.md.
findings.note: new finding at 8d299b8d; grep-verified that neither scripts/license-gate.mjs nor scripts/audit-gate.mjs reads the expires field.

findings.title: Deploy verifies the tag's attestation but pulls by mutable tag; the SBOM predicate is never verified
evidence: .github/workflows/deploy-do.yml:501-514 — verify-attestations resolves the pushed tag to a digest and runs `gh attestation verify` with --signer-workflow/--source-digest (no --predicate-type)
.github/workflows/deploy-do.yml:786-788 — the deploy step then pulls ghcr.io/.../mct-api:${IMAGE_TAG} by mutable tag; infra/digitalocean/docker-compose.yml:69,131,187 reference the same :${IMAGE_TAG}
docs/SBOM_PROCESS.md:120-135 — documents a stricter manual check (--predicate-type https://cyclonedx.org/bom) that CI does not run
docs/SBOM_PROCESS.md:159-174 — claims the job 'proves each image that deploy is about to pull was built by THIS repository'
findings.impact: A GHCR writer (or a compromised job holding packages:write) can re-point the commit-SHA tag after verification and the deploy will pull and run the substituted image — the original CTR-P1-003 substitution threat is narrowed but not closed. Because `gh attestation verify` is not given --predicate-type, the gate does not require the build-provenance predicate (or the SBOM predicate) specifically; either attestation type satisfies it.
findings.recommendation: Have verify-attestations output the resolved digests and pass them to the deploy job; pull and run by @sha256:... (compose image with digest), or re-resolve + re-verify the digest on the droplet immediately after pull. Add --predicate-type checks for both SLSA provenance and the CycloneDX SBOM predicate, and validate the SBOM content.
findings.note: new finding at 8d299b8d; hits the extended check 'no post-signing additions in the release set'. Exploit requires registry write access, but the fix is cheap (digest-pinned pull).

findings.title: No scheduled dependency vulnerability re-scan — advisories are only evaluated on PRs and deploys
evidence: .github/actions/dependency-audit/action.yml:12-17 — the vulnerability gate (scripts/audit-gate.mjs) is only invoked from test.yml:52 (pull_request) and validate.yml:17 (deploy gate, reached via deploy-do.yml push)
.github/workflows/sbom.yml:8-9 — the only weekly dependency-related schedule generates/validates the SBOM but never runs the audit gate
.github/workflows/codeql.yml:8-9 — weekly schedule exists but covers code scanning, not dependency advisories
no workflow in .github/workflows/ references scripts/audit-gate.mjs on a schedule (grep cron + audit-gate)
findings.impact: If no PR or deploy happens for weeks, an advisory published against the unchanged resolved tree is invisible to CI. GitHub Dependabot alerts may cover this, but that is a repository setting and cannot be verified from the repo.
findings.recommendation: Add a weekly scheduled job that runs `node scripts/audit-gate.mjs` (enforcing) or `--report` plus a deduplicated issue (pattern: secret-rotation-reminder.yml), or document explicitly that Dependabot security alerts are the compensating control and record the last triage date.
findings.note: new finding at 8d299b8d; repo-side evidence is complete, but whether GitHub Dependabot security alerts are enabled is not visible in the repository (marked medium confidence).

findings.title: Image SBOMs are attested but never validated (no floor or binding check)
evidence: scripts/validate-sbom.mjs:56-61 — component floor and binding checks exist, but only for the lockfile document (docs/SBOM_PROCESS.md:95-100 states it is not run against the Trivy image SBOMs)
.github/workflows/deploy-do.yml:220-243 — the Trivy image SBOM is attested immediately after generation; no validation step in between
.github/workflows/build-push.yml:64-83 — the image SBOM is uploaded as an artifact with no validation
docs/SBOM_PROCESS.md:36-53 — the binding fields to assert (metadata.component.purl/name = ...@sha256:..., aquasecurity:trivy:RepoDigest)
findings.impact: A Trivy/SBOM regression that emits an empty or partial image SBOM would still be attested and stored as the durable record for that digest, defeating the purpose of the attestation.
findings.recommendation: Add a small validator for the image SBOM (non-empty components, expected component classes present, metadata.component.purl contains the image digest) and run it before attest-sbom / upload; reuse the check in both workflows.
findings.note: new finding at 8d299b8d; direct code evidence (no validation step between generation and attestation).

findings.title: Runbooks and script headers still document the broken `pnpm licenses list --json` command; docs/CI.md SBOM row is stale
evidence: docs/SBOM_PROCESS.md:116 and docs/DEPENDENCY_POLICY.md:77 — local runbooks instruct `pnpm licenses list --json > licenses.json`
scripts/license-gate.mjs:16,30 and scripts/generate-sbom.mjs:11,258 — usage/headers describe the same command as the input source

.github/workflows/sbom.yml:36-47 and scripts/collect-licenses.mjs:5-19 — document that on the pinned pnpm@10.34.3 (package.json packageManager) this exact command exits 1 and writes an error document to stdout, which is why CI switched to collect-licenses.mjs
docs/SBOM_PROCESS.md:26 — still says per-component licenses are 'sourced from `pnpm licenses list --json`'
docs/CI.md:29 — the SBOM row still says image SBOMs are emitted by build-push.yml (deploy-do.yml also emits and attests them)
findings.impact: An operator or future agent following the runbook produces a licenses.json containing an error object and then sees the license gate or SBOM generation fail (or produce an SBOM without licenses) locally — a documented procedure that does not work as written.
findings.recommendation: Replace the command with `node scripts/collect-licenses.mjs --out licenses.json` in both docs and in the two script headers; update docs/SBOM_PROCESS.md:26 and docs/CI.md:29 to match the implemented pipeline.
findings.note: new finding at 8d299b8d; the command's failure mode is documented in-repo. It could not be reproduced literally (no node/pnpm runtime on the audit host).

findings.title: Documented sharp license exception does not match the machine policy
evidence: docs/LICENSE_POLICY.md:50 — table row excepts `Apache-2.0 AND LGPL-3.0-or-later` for `@img/sharp-win32-x64`
security/license-policy.json:79-81 — the actual exception key is the bare `LGPL-3.0-or-later` scoped (in text) to `@img/sharp-libvips-linux-x64`
.github/workflows/dependency-review.yml:28 — comment repeats the Windows purl / expression pairing

scripts/license-gate.mjs:54-63 — an expression whose leaf hits the deny list fails; `Apache-2.0 AND LGPL-3.0-or-later` is not an exception key, so it would be denied if the Windows package were ever installed (e.g. a Windows contributor or a supportedArchitectures change)
findings.impact: The documented exception does not protect the documented case: the machine policy and the human table disagree about the license string and the package. A non-Linux run of the license gate can fail with no obvious remediation, and reviewers cannot trust the table as the policy of record.
findings.recommendation: Make the exception key match the real reported license string(s) and implement package scoping (see the exception-matching finding); then regenerate the docs table from security/license-policy.json, or add a CI check that the two artifacts list the same (license, package) pairs.
findings.note: new finding at 8d299b8d; the artifact mismatch is certain (docs vs JSON vs dependency-review comment). The exact license string reported for the Windows binary was not reproduced (node_modules absent, no install allowed).

findings.title: Shipped third-party images and GitHub Actions dependencies have no SBOM coverage

# SBOM and License Policy Audit

## Audit Metadata

- Audit name: `repo-deep-dive`
- Run: `mainecybertech-20261011-0426-full-main-8d299b8`
- Repository: `mainecybertech` (MaineCyberTech portal monorepo)

- Commit SHA: `8d299b8dc271c410b9ae2ceeda3d2c6c997af8fd` (2026-10-11 00:13:46 -0400, "Merge PR #168: promote develop to main")

- Output path: `docs/audits/repo-deep-dive/mainecybertech-20261011-0426-full-main-8d299b8/35_sbom_license_policy.md`

Live GHCR attestations were not queried.

## Scope

Reviewed: package manifests and license fields; `pnpm-lock.yaml`; Dockerfiles and both compose files; GitHub Actions workflows and composite actions (SBOM, dependency review, build/push, deploy, validate, test, CodeQL); dependency-update config; the SBOM generator/validator and license/audit gates; the license and dependency-audit policies; the SBOM, license, dependency, CI and release documentation; release provenance/signing; the exception process.

Not reviewed here (owned by other domains): image digest pinning policy and Dockerfile lint (container runtime security), secret scanning/rotation, and the CI workflow topology itself.

## Executive Summary

The domain has moved a long way from the prior full run. The lockfile SBOM is CycloneDX 1.5, commit- and version-bound, carries per-component licenses and a dependency graph, and is validated by a regression guard before upload (`sbom.yml:35-60`). Every shipped image gets a Trivy CycloneDX SBOM bound to its pushed digest and attested into the registry (`deploy-do.yml:220-243` and siblings), build provenance is attested and **verified fail-closed before deploy** (`verify-attestations`), and a real license allow/deny policy now runs on every PR and on the deploy gate over the full resolved tree (`license-gate.mjs` + `security/license-policy.json` + the `dependency-audit` composite). Generated aggregates stay untracked by policy and by guard. All GitHub Actions are SHA-pinned and Dependabot covers npm, actions, docker and terraform.

The remaining risk is not absence but **contract fidelity**. The license exceptions are matched by license string only, so the documented per-package scoping is not enforced and the `UNKNOWN` exception lets any unlicensed package pass both gates. Exception `expires` dates are decoration — neither gate reads them. On the provenance side, the deploy verifies the tag→digest attestation and then pulls the **mutable tag**, so a registry writer could substitute the artifact after verification; the SBOM predicate is never explicitly verified. Image SBOMs are attested without any completeness/binding validation, third-party runtime images (redis, caddy, prometheus, alertmanager) and the Actions dependencies have no SBOM coverage, and there is no scheduled re-scan of the resolved tree against newly published advisories. Documentation drift (broken `pnpm licenses list` command in runbooks/headers, a sharp exception that does not exist in the machine policy, a stale CI.md row) will mislead the next operator or agent.

Verdict: the pipeline is **functionally strong (score ~4/5) but not yet trustworthy as an audit artifact** until exception scoping/expiry, digest-pinned deployment, image-SBOM validation and the scheduled advisory scan are fixed. No P0/P1 issues were found at this commit; the previously filed P1s are verified fixed except the release-identity residual (partially fixed).

### Item: Lockfile SBOM generation and binding

- Current controls: validation before upload (format, unique refs, dangling refs, floor 100, binding); CI regenerates it on push/PR/weekly.
- Missing controls: no durable storage for the lockfile SBOM (30-day artifact); no release attachment.

### Item: Image SBOMs and attestation

- Evidence: `deploy-do.yml:220-243,286-304,355-373`; `build-push.yml:64-90,135-160,216-241`; `docs/SBOM_PROCESS.md:36-63`.

### New findings (9 rows)

#### SBOM-P2 (new) — License exceptions are matched by license string only; documented package scope and UNKNOWN fail open

- Severity: P2 · Confidence: high · Status: open
- Evidence: `scripts/license-gate.mjs:37-39,50-53` (exceptions keyed by license; `entry.packages` never read); `security/license-policy.json:87-92` (`UNKNOWN` exception for browser-assert → blanket pass for every unlicensed package); `docs/LICENSE_POLICY.md:44-45` claims per-package scoping that the code does not implement; pinned `dependency-review-action` `src/licenses.ts` reports unlicensed deps without failing.
- What is happening: any new dependency whose license string equals an exception key passes without review, and any package with no license field passes both gates.
- Why it matters: the compliance control does not implement its documented contract; a future MPL-2.0 / LGPL-3.0-or-later / FSL / unlicensed dependency merges unreviewed.
- Recommended fix: match on (license, package name); fail UNKNOWN unless the package is explicitly listed; update JSON comment and docs; add unit fixtures.
- Owner/effort: supply-chain owner · S–M

#### SBOM-P2 (new) — Exception `expires` dates are documentation-only

- Severity: P2 · Confidence: high · Status: open
- Evidence: `security/license-policy.json:66,76,84,92`; `security/dependency-audit-policy.json:16`; neither `scripts/license-gate.mjs` nor `scripts/audit-gate.mjs` references `expires` (grep); `docs/DEPENDENCY_POLICY.md:30` promises an expiry.
- Why it matters: accepted risks outlive their review with no failing signal (the only removal hint is when the license string vanishes — never for UNKNOWN).
- Recommended fix: parse ISO dates and fail/warn when past due; add a past-date fixture test.
- Owner/effort: supply-chain owner · S

#### SBOM-P2 (new) — Deploy verifies the tag's attestation but pulls by mutable tag; SBOM predicate never verified

- Severity: P2 · Confidence: high · Status: open

- Why it matters: post-signing substitution (re-pointing the commit tag) defeats the stated guarantee; the SBOM predicate could be absent while verification still passes. Direct hit on the "no post-signing additions" extended check.
- Recommended fix: pass resolved digests from `verify-attestations` to the deploy and pull/run by digest (or re-verify on the droplet); add `--predicate-type` checks for provenance and SBOM.
- Owner/effort: platform/infrastructure · M

#### SBOM-P2 (new) — No scheduled dependency vulnerability re-scan

- Severity: P2 · Confidence: medium · Status: open
- Evidence: `dependency-audit` composite (`action.yml:12-17`) is only invoked from `test.yml:52` (PR) and `validate.yml:17` (deploy gate); `sbom.yml:8-9` is weekly but never runs the audit; `codeql.yml:8-9` is code scanning.
- Why it matters: advisories published while the tree is unchanged stay invisible to CI; Dependabot alerts may cover it but are not repo-verifiable.
- Recommended fix: weekly scheduled `audit-gate.mjs` (or report + dedup issue), or document Dependabot alerts as the compensating control with a triage date.
- Owner/effort: supply-chain owner · S

#### SBOM-P3 (new) — Image SBOMs are attested but never validated

- Severity: P3 · Confidence: high · Status: open
- Evidence: `validate-sbom.mjs:56-61` + `SBOM_PROCESS.md:95-100` (lockfile only); `deploy-do.yml:220-243` attests with no validation step; `build-push.yml:64-83` uploads unvalidated.
- Why it matters: an empty/partial image SBOM would be attested and retained as the durable record for that digest.
- Recommended fix: small validator (component floor, expected classes, digest in `metadata.component.purl`) run before attest/upload.
- Owner/effort: platform/infrastructure · S
